packet.objective: Wire the GitHub provider into native PM shipping and prove the complete remote lifecycle

acceptance.text: PM remote adapter pushes scoped branches, creates/updates PRs and merges only exact verified heads with passing required checks under standing authorization; fake remote tests cover missing auth, pending/failure, races and merge result mismatch without real remote/model calls.

Actual CLI/API wiring consumes fresh source and integration evidence, reconciles provider merge/squash/rebase lineage and advanced integration tip only with real Git proof, and performs P/E/H closure under standing authority. Unsupported or pending states stay explicit without resetting claims or budgets.

Fake provider and real temporary Git repositories exercise full publish, readiness, exact merge, integration gates, reporting where required, merged Execution and fresh-process handoff; no disconnected helper is presented as an implemented user operation.

findings.message: current-pm.mjs validateAdmissionRecord/remoteAdmissionStatus accepts syntactically coherent completion without the required remote proof chain. It checks remote.version, optional slots only if present, completion target/branch/commit, then marks COMPLETE when commit is ancestor of HEAD. A record can omit source publication/merge proof, integration_evidence finalization, closure/handoff-repair proof and terminal artifact identities yet release admission. This directly violates initial-observations admission-proof ('syntactically valid completion.status alone cannot release hold').

closure/repair provider interruption is not implemented. reconcileExecutingAttempt is called only by source publish/merge. Closure executeProviderAttempt leaves thrown executing slots stuck; closure reconcile proves Git without settling the slot. Repair uses a bespoke runner that unconditionally allocates a new token whenever effect is null, overwriting an executing active token and permitting a second write; repair reconcile also never settles slots. This violates the all-stage prepared/executing/observed and read-only recovery contract. Fresh-process lost execution must remain UNKNOWN absent exact effect adoption; same-process ended+exact absence may replay the same token.

raced closure preimage checks compare only file text/hash, not Git mode. A concurrent 100644→100755 mode change on a P/E/H path has identical committedText, is allowed as an in-scope changed path, then wrapper restores H's mode; code accepts it, overwriting the advanced-base entry despite exact-preimage requirement.

H2 adoption compares only captureGitAnchor().protected_hash; unlike closure/completion it retains no protectedIgnoredEntries checkout proof, so worktree-local ignored protected metadata can drift between prepare/adopt without refusal.

maybeSupersedeSourceAttempt changes old.disposition/superseded_by then refreshAttempt(old), but deliberately leaves slot.effect unchanged. Its effect.attempt_identity therefore points to the pre-mutation identity that no retained attempt now has. The supersession proof omits required predecessor attempt/effect identities and validateProviderSlot never checks reciprocal links/effect-to-attempt binding. After successor success old effect pointer is replaced, so old identity is not durably recoverable.

rebase proof sets rebaseBase=parents[0] of final rebased commit and checks only rebaseBase..mergeCommit; for legitimate multi-commit source rebase, that parent is the preceding rebased source commit, so earlier rebased commits are outside bounded-path proof. Established premerge base is retained in merge attempt observation and should anchor the whole first-parent range. Current tests use one source commit.

claimCurrentPm checks remote admission before entering transact but does not repeat it inside the transaction, contrary to the approved T05B admission dispatch. A remote record can become applicable in another checkout after the precheck and before the story write, and the claim then commits without the required hold.

validateRemoteEnvelope validates only provider-slot shells and retry range, while prepareRemoteClosureCheckout trusts truthy integration_evidence.finalized/finalization. It does not validate the identified finalization or its binding to the current snapshot, gates, review and verification; a malformed/rebound record can therefore enter P/E/H closure with forged finalized evidence.

source merge interruption treats `MERGE_PENDING` as an absence state eligible for same-process replay (`mergeRemoteSource` passes `absenceStates: ['MERGE_PENDING']`). The frozen dispatch says replay requires exact provider absence and that open/queued remains pending; an open/queued PR may already retain a provider merge request, so it cannot prove no effect and must not authorize a second merge write. This needs to stay pending/read-only unless exact merge effect is adopted.

prepareRemoteHandoff does not require an adopted story-closure E. remotePrepareArtifact assigns `parent = closure.commit`, which can be null, persists the handoff pending record, then writes H bytes. Adoption can never accept a real commit whose parent equals null, and the dirty H write then prevents preparing E, leaving the workflow wedged. The public operation should refuse before record/file mutation until E is adopted.

prepareHandoffRepair is not resumable across its own durable-preparation/file-write boundary. It first records a prepared attempt in withRecord, writes H2 bytes afterward, but every repeated prepare rejects whenever latest exists without race_proof. A crash after record persistence and before/while writeArtifact therefore cannot apply the retained pending after-image or return its token; the accepted prepare/adopt interruption model is broken.

Premerge supersession still violates the frozen qualification rules. integration.mjs:1940-1966 can supersede source publication after a successful source merge because it never checks the merge effect/proof; it also accepts PR_DRAFT, CHECKS_PENDING and CHECKS_FAILED as qualifying current observations. remoteObservation at 1928-1934 uses `result.remoteBase || observedRemoteBase(...)`, treating an explicitly null provider base like an omitted field. The dispatch requires successful merge to forbid supersession, pending/failed observations to remain read-only, and fallback only when remoteBase is absent. Add the merge-terminal veto, restrict the qualifying current states, and distinguish an absent property from a present invalid/null value before allocating a successor.

The persisted provider-attempt validator checks transition identities and previous pointers but not the required state machine. At state.mjs:103-118, an observed attempt can be changed from prepared→executing→observed to prepared→observed by removing executing, rebinding observed.previous and reidentifying that transition; stable attempt identity and effect binding still validate, so terminal admission accepts evidence without a retained executing boundary. Enforce first prepared, prepared→executing, executing→observed with the same invocation token, and executing→prepared only with an exact replay proof; also bind active token and disposition to the legal terminal state.

Remote artifact interruption recovery does not require the retained clean checkout. After remote-close-prepare persists E, restore the owned story to pending.before, make an unrelated unstaged change such as src/unrelated.txt, then call remote-close-prepare with the retained hash. remotePrepareArtifact passes clean:false for pending state and applyPending checks only the owned story, so it writes E and returns the old token amid unrelated work. H2 resume has the same gap because its anchor comparison does not cover unstaged ordinary worktree changes. The contract requires exact interruption state and preservation of unrelated work. Validate the retained pending shape and generated P/E/H or H2 image, require status to contain only the owned pending paths, and on unrelated status refuse with both owned and unrelated bytes unchanged.

Terminal publication proof remains incompletely cross-bound. state.mjs:352-359 accepts handoff_repair.proof without requiring its retained pr_number to be a positive integer equal to the effect-bound merge attempt input.prNumber. For a normal closure, state.mjs:313-323 allows state `proven` while terminal_commit differs from the provider-bound merge_commit; rebinding that proof and completion together to a later commit that preserves the story/handoff entries can release admission even though the exact provider R was different. Require the repair PR equality and require a proven normal closure terminal to equal its merge effect commit.

Normal merge and squash reconciliation still use record.integration.base I as the provider base, while rebase correctly uses the effect-bound attempt's retained remote_observation.observed_remote_base. If the remote integration branch advances from I to proved N before the provider merge, a valid merge result with ordered parents [N,C] and exact merge-tree(N,C), or a valid squash direct child of N with that bounded source composition, is rejected at reconcileRemoteSource. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:17 require proof against the uniquely established provider base and fresh evidence at the resulting fetched M. Derive N from the merge effect's retained observation for every method, validate it as the exact proved base, and use it for parent, bounded delta and recomputed-tree checks.

mergeRemoteSource does not implement the fix2 terminal fast path. After a source merge effect or source proof exists, it still calls remoteObservation/provider.inspect before executeProviderAttempt returns the retained effect. A same-input completed merge therefore depends on fresh provider and Git reads and can fail when the provider is unavailable, despite already having a durable result. T05B-fix2-design.json and T05B-supersession-dispatch.md require the successful merge to veto inspection, allocation and writes while preserving the same-input proven result.

Handoff-repair replacements generate a stale BASE_COMMIT. After HANDOFF_BASE_RACE, prepareHandoffRepair correctly selects latest.race_proof.terminal_commit as the new repairBase and pending parent, but remoteArtifactGeneration still receives closureCommit=closure.terminal_commit. The public retry therefore creates H2 as a direct child of the latest N while its handoff bytes name the original closure terminal. Resume and adoption repeat the same stale generation input, and completion later refuses the result. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:31 requires each replacement H2 to use BASE_COMMIT N for its actual latest proved parent.

Remote verification-report preparation can overwrite existing project reports. architecture-state.md:216 says P adds only docs/verification/<story-id>.md and docs/checklists/verification-<story-id>.md, and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:25 retains the existing P contract. prepareRemoteVerificationReport passes those paths to materializeRemoteWrites, which accepts non-null committed before-images. When a fetched advanced M already contains either path, the public P operation replaces it instead of refusing before durable preparation.

Remote artifact generation is not independently bound to its parent or retained after adoption. validateRemoteGeneration regenerates report/closure bytes from generation.inputs.story_before supplied by the descriptor itself but never requires that story to equal the committed parent story or pending write.before, nor does it require the retained source contract/execution identity. A coherently reidentified same-contract, different-Execution descriptor can therefore resume and adopt an E that is not the legal transition from its parent. remoteAdoptArtifact then discards the generation descriptor and records only field/commit/parent/tree/writes, so terminal P/E/H proof no longer names the source proof or remote finalization that generated it. This violates remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 and :25, which require receipts and closure preparation to remain bound to fetched M and its finalization.

Remote artifact publication does not preserve executable Git mode. materializeRemoteWrites retains expected_mode, but applyPending writes through atomic, whose replacement file is created mode 0600, and never restores the owner's executable bit. A valid 100755 story or handoff therefore becomes 100644 during E, H or H2 preparation and cannot pass adoption's exact expected-mode check. Pending recovery also compares only text, so same-text executable-mode drift on an owned path is accepted as resumable. The existing P/E/H entry contract and remote state schema explicitly support both 100644 and 100755.

Remote terminal evidence validation does not establish exact acceptance coverage or independent actors. validateRemotePublicationRecord accepts any nonempty all-PASS verification criteria without matching their IDs exactly to source.packet.acceptance, and it does not enforce that the remote reviewer and verifier differ from the builder and each other or that required panel coverage remains present. Reidentifying a same-snapshot verification with one invented PASS criterion and colliding actors still permits finalization, closure and terminal admission. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 require fresh independent review and distinct complete verification bound to M.

A retained provider replay proof is not bound to the attempt target. validateRemoteProviderSlot checks that replay.absence_result is identified PR_ABSENT evidence and binds its invocation token, but does not require absence_result.expectedHead to equal attempt.input.target.expectedHead. A reidentified replay transition can therefore claim exact absence for a different head and later support a terminal provider chain. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:9 requires exact attempt inputs and result identity before same-token replay.

remoteAdmissionStatus reports the wrong terminal field before completion preparation. It selects value.remote.closure.proof.commit, but remote-closure-proof-v1 retains merge_commit and terminal_commit. A normal or stale REMOTE_CLOSURE_PROVEN record consequently returns remote_terminal_commit:null until a completion token exists, contrary to the exact remote-admission-status projection in T05B-operation-dispatch.md.

The declared npm test gate did not complete for the frozen fix2 candidate: it terminated with ETIMEDOUT at 600 seconds. Packaging validation passed, the candidate snapshot remained unchanged, and no orphan test processes remained, but a timed-out gate is not a PASS and cannot establish T05B acceptance.

A source merge attempted while checks are pending cannot persist its exact observed result. remote.mjs returns CHECKS_PENDING before issuing a merge write, executeProviderAttempt appends an observed transition with active disposition, and state.mjs rejects that legal no-effect state as 'source merge unresolved attempt has effect'. The record remains at executing. Later calls only return PENDING from read-only reconciliation, even after checks become ready, so the source lifecycle is wedged without any merge command having run.

An observed MERGE_PENDING result cannot later be reconciled to the exact server merge. The pending observation clears active_token and retains no effect. mergeRemoteSource then replays the retained PENDING result, while reconcileRemoteSource settles only an active executing attempt. When the provider later returns MERGED, reconcileRemoteSource builds the Git proof but state validation rejects source.proof because source.merge.effect is still absent. This violates the required same-attempt queue-completion reconciliation.

Remote evidence can still be reset after the closure checkout is prepared. prepareRemoteClosureCheckout checks finalization once, but assertRemoteEvidenceMutable freezes evidence only after an artifact is pending or committed. A later gate, review or verification clears finalization. P or E preparation then persists an artifact generation with finalization null; adoption rejects it, while the pending artifact prevents evidence from being finalized again. The lifecycle is permanently wedged.

A real handoff-repair base race before the provider merge is not retained as HANDOFF_BASE_RACE. If the provider wrapper has parents [advanced-N,H2], reconcileRemoteHandoffRepair requires parents [attempt.parent,H2] and throws before writing race_proof or spending a bounded replacement retry. The adopted attempt then has neither proof nor race_proof, and prepareHandoffRepair cannot resume or allocate a replacement.

Checkout-free terminal receipt validation does not enforce the recording API's review summary type and 8000-character bound. A coherently reidentified stored review can therefore contain a non-string or oversized summary and still pass validateRemotePublicationRecord, up to the broader integration-record byte limit.

review.summary: FAIL. The fix3 repairs resolve all 25 findings from review-T05B-fix2, and the frozen snapshot has passing npm test and packaging gates. Four current lifecycle defects remain. Pending checks wedge source merge before any provider write; an observed queued merge cannot acquire the effect needed for later exact reconciliation; evidence reset after closure-checkout preparation leaves an unadoptable artifact that also freezes re-finalization; and a true pre-merge H2 base race throws before durable race evidence and bounded replacement. The coordinator's disposable reproduction independently reproduced the first two defects in .deliver/checkpoints/T05B-fix3-candidate/fable-current-repro.log. The fresh-process replay objection was not retained because the approved fix2 contract explicitly permits replay only with same-process ended proof. The source premerge-N objection was not retained because the exact retained premerge-N rule is pinned by the approved design.

criteria.evidence: Frozen snapshot 232f5d3e1c04cf155b6b0c96f85f988dec93c9588f6a2a70a2b9d7ef165a88d2 matches the manifest hashes. In remote.mjs, publish pushes only EXPECTED_HEAD:refs/heads/STORY_BRANCH at lines 599-617; merge requires READY checks, rechecks the exact PR, and invokes gh with --match-head-commit at lines 672-704; open queue results remain MERGE_PENDING and postmerge identity/base mismatches do not report completion. tests/remote.test.mjs uses an injected fake runner and contains explicit missing-auth, pending/failed/unknown-check, changed-head race, rejected/queued merge, merge mismatch, and read-only exact/advanced reconciliation cases. The exact-snapshot npm test receipt is PASS with 349/349 tests, 0 failures, duration 486440.215083 ms, log SHA-256 c9d9db3a032c7b3118c6db27076ca91bb4c46d2776429878a597362e0c501299; npm run validate is PASS with log SHA-256 6e13c61ea3c623487770df0fd4a6c35da4a9cb8a72bea51a94775f591e10ad88. post-gate-check.json retains the same snapshot at revision 19.

Current source has reachable lifecycle failures despite the green declared gates. First, executeProviderAttempt records PR_DRAFT/CHECKS_PENDING/CHECKS_FAILED as observed with active disposition and no effect at integration.mjs:1859-1873, while state.mjs:202-207 rejects that exact state as 'unresolved attempt has effect'; the current-snapshot reproduction log records pending-check merge throwing that error and remaining stuck when checks become ready. Second, MERGE_PENDING is retained as observed without an effect, but reconcileRemoteSource only settles an active_token at integration.mjs:2158-2169 and later writes source proof without creating the required merge effect; state.mjs:377-391 rejects it. The same raw reproduction records a later real server merge failing with 'source proof binding'. Third, reconcileRemoteHandoffRepair checks exact [attempt.parent,H2] parents at integration.mjs:3026-3028 before its fetched-tip race branch at :3029, so a true provider-side premerge base advance throws instead of retaining HANDOFF_BASE_RACE and spending the bounded replacement retry required by remote-lifecycle-interface.md:31. Fourth, prepareRemoteClosureCheckout at :2392-2407 retains no finalization identity, assertRemoteEvidenceMutable at :2457-2459 freezes only after an artifact starts, and gate/review/verification operations may clear finalization at :2326/:2341/:2357. Artifact preparation at :2601-2628 does not re-require finalized evidence, so it can persist a generation with null finalization and then wedge adoption while freezing further evidence repair. These are current source defects, not the stale external receipt. The external objections to fresh-process replay and to replacing effect-bound premerge N do not establish failures: T05B-operation-dispatch.md:53 explicitly permits replay only after same-process ended proof, and T05B-fix2-design-preflight-native.json:14 explicitly defines N as the effect-bound premerge observation.

The 349-test gate exercises many real temporary-Git and fake-provider paths, but it does not demonstrate the complete required lifecycle on the current implementation. Its logged queue case is only 'queued merge observation cannot replay an ended merge invocation'; the current-snapshot defect reproduction at .deliver/checkpoints/T05B-fix3-candidate/fable-current-repro.log, SHA-256 f4e1910db93598ea56365f96ded451f69e685b8375850d6ea0b943f18af11e18, proves both the pending-check durable-state failure and failure to adopt a later queued merge. The H2 implementation rejects a true base race before recording race_proof, and closure checkout permits finalization invalidation before P/E/H preparation. Therefore the passing suite does not prove queue completion, true H2/S replacement after a provider-side premerge race, or immutable finalization through checkout and artifact preparation. Those missing working paths are expressly required by remote-lifecycle-interface.md:47 and prevent a full publish-through-fresh-process-handoff acceptance.

details.reason: Address the eleven independent T05B round1 major findings and failed AC2/AC3 with retained regression coverage. Preserve original task, baseline and existing evidence; this is fix round 1.

review.summary: Reviewed the complete frozen T05B scope at snapshot 89d174d040b90ceeb474576fc53939086084ecbd1466be08f0653a51c13fac1d against the original three acceptance criteria, approved remote contracts and dispatch notes, all 13 initial observations, the rebase ruling, retained Fable triage, production wiring and frozen tests. The declared gates passed unchanged: npm test 340/340 in 563301.498166ms and validate PASS. The CLI and installed complete-operation routing are connected, fetch/push identity is enforced, empty rebase commits are correctly permitted, required-check absence is explicitly diagnosed, and retained strict PR/CLEAN behavior matches policy. The eleven unresolved major findings leave AC1, AC2 and AC3 unproved despite the passing gates.

criteria.evidence: At frozen snapshot 89d174d040b90ceeb474576fc53939086084ecbd1466be08f0653a51c13fac1d, I inspected remote.mjs and its frozen SHA-256 ba21914d8a131532ec38c66e40948621da9d81452449024d59ba5a837a10ea89. The adapter validates one identical fetch/push GitHub destination and active auth; pushes only `EXPECTED:refs/heads/BRANCH` without force/tracking/config; creates or edits the exact repository/head/base PR; requires exact head, structured required checks and a fresh CLEAN/MERGEABLE view; invokes `gh pr merge` with `--match-head-commit`; and returns MERGED only after a full merge OID and exact remote-base match. Frozen remote.test.mjs covers unavailable/auth/lookup distinctions, pending/failed/unknown checks, head races, rejected/queued/mismatched merges and already-merged read-only reconciliation using an injected runner. The declared gate passed 340/340 with no failures; test log SHA-256 48c78552418eaa7fa14fb4651b8c78332ab5b65695fdbd1ddf694c4983d4a2f2. No real provider/model call is present in these tests.

Actual CLI functions exist, but the frozen lifecycle does not meet the required proof and pending-state contract. First, current-pm.mjs:324-343 validates only record binding, any slots that happen to exist and a minimal completion tuple; :392-395 releases nonblocking COMPLETE solely when completion.commit is an ancestor of HEAD. It does not require source publication/merge effects, source Git proof, finalized remote-M gates/review/verification, closure/repair proof, or exact retained terminal story/handoff artifacts, so syntactically coherent incomplete evidence can release claims. Second, integration.mjs:2167-2183 sets the rebase range start to the final commit's immediate parent, so it inspects only the final edge: I→U(add unauthorized)→V(revert to I tree)→M(apply exact source delta) can pass without examining U/V, contrary to the whole bounded first-parent contract. Third, source merge recovery at :2074-2077 treats MERGE_PENDING as exact absence and can replay a queued merge; closure and repair provider writes lack the generic executing-attempt reconciliation, with closure stuck as PROVIDER_EXECUTING after a lost process and repair able to allocate another attempt. These violate remote-lifecycle-interface.md:9, :17 and :41-43. Passing gates do not establish these omitted boundaries.

The frozen fake-provider/temporary-Git suite does exercise happy-path publish/readiness/merge, fresh remote-M gates/review/verification, P/E/H, raced closure/H2/S, completion and next-story admission, and the operation map exposes `complete`; npm test passed 340/340 in 563301.498166ms and npm run validate passed, validation log SHA-256 4750e94bf4d841f7f53f054413e9df9e5055fbbb25a1d53edfa18c366a54f89b. Scope is clean across ten authorized changed paths. However, its admission negatives alter only completion.commit or add a copied record and never remove/rebind the required proof chain; its rebase negative uses one unauthorized intermediate whose deletion occurs on the inspected final edge, not a separately reverted earlier edge; and interruption tests cover source slots only. Thus the suite does not exercise the full required lifecycle boundaries, and the inspected source admits premature completion, hidden rebase history and unresolved/duplicated closure or repair provider attempts. Builder recover_t05c, test author correction_regressions and verifier correction_verifier are distinct, but the criterion remains failed on functionality and coverage.

details.reason: Fix1 whole-task review reports five residual remote lifecycle defects despite 345 passing tests: supersession qualification, provider transition legality, artifact interruption status, terminal proof cross-links, and advanced premerge-base merge/squash proof. Preserve all prior findings, original task and baseline.

A crash after record persistence and before/while writeArtifact therefore cannot apply the retained pending after-image or return its token; the accepted prepare/adopt interruption model is broken.

Premerge supersession still violates the frozen qualification rules. integration.mjs:1940-1966 can supersede source publication after a successful source merge because it never checks the merge effect/proof; it also accepts PR_DRAFT, CHECKS_PENDING and CHECKS_FAILED as qualifying current observations. remoteObservation at 1928-1934 uses `result.remoteBase || observedRemoteBase(...)`, treating an explicitly null provider base like an omitted field. The dispatch requires successful merge to forbid supersession, pending/failed observations to remain read-only, and fallback only when remoteBase is absent. Add the merge-terminal veto, restrict the qualifying current states, and distinguish an absent property from a present invalid/null value before allocating a successor.

The persisted provider-attempt validator checks transition identities and previous pointers but not the required state machine. At state.mjs:103-118, an observed attempt can be changed from prepared→executing→observed to prepared→observed by removing executing, rebinding observed.previous and reidentifying that transition; stable attempt identity and effect binding still validate, so terminal admission accepts evidence without a retained executing boundary. Enforce first prepared, prepared→executing, executing→observed with the same invocation token, and executing→prepared only with an exact replay proof; also bind active token and disposition to the legal terminal state.

Remote artifact interruption recovery does not require the retained clean checkout. After remote-close-prepare persists E, restore the owned story to pending.before, make an unrelated unstaged change such as src/unrelated.txt, then call remote-close-prepare with the retained hash. remotePrepareArtifact passes clean:false for pending state and applyPending checks only the owned story, so it writes E and returns the old token amid unrelated work. H2 resume has the same gap because its anchor comparison does not cover unstaged ordinary worktree changes. The contract requires exact interruption state and preservation of unrelated work. Validate the retained pending shape and generated P/E/H or H2 image, require status to contain only the owned pending paths, and on unrelated status refuse with both owned and unrelated bytes unchanged.

Terminal publication proof remains incompletely cross-bound. state.mjs:352-359 accepts handoff_repair.proof without requiring its retained pr_number to be a positive integer equal to the effect-bound merge attempt input.prNumber. For a normal closure, state.mjs:313-323 allows state `proven` while terminal_commit differs from the provider-bound merge_commit; rebinding that proof and completion together to a later commit that preserves the story/handoff entries can release admission even though the exact provider R was different. Require the repair PR equality and require a proven normal closure terminal to equal its merge effect commit.

Normal merge and squash reconciliation still use record.integration.base I as the provider base, while rebase correctly uses the effect-bound attempt's retained remote_observation.observed_remote_base. If the remote integration branch advances from I to proved N before the provider merge, a valid merge result with ordered parents [N,C] and exact merge-tree(N,C), or a valid squash direct child of N with that bounded source composition, is rejected at reconcileRemoteSource. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:17 require proof against the uniquely established provider base and fresh evidence at the resulting fetched M. Derive N from the merge effect's retained observation for every method, validate it as the exact proved base, and use it for parent, bounded delta and recomputed-tree checks.

The eleven round-one defects are addressed in the inspected source: terminal admission now requires the source/evidence/closure-or-repair/completion chain and terminal Git bytes/modes; claim rechecks admission inside its transaction; rebase proof uses the retained premerge base and every bounded first-parent edge; P/E/H modes and H2 protected ignored metadata are checked; closure and repair use prepared/executing/observed reconciliation; fresh-process absence stays PROVIDER_UNKNOWN; MERGE_PENDING does not replay; finalized-M evidence is validated; H requires adopted E; and H2 preparation resumes retained before/after images. One public exact-proof defect remains. reconcileRemoteHandoffRepair accepts caller prNumber and persists it as handoff_repair.proof.pr_number at integration.mjs:2777-2807. If a retained repair merge effect was produced for PR X, a reconciliation of PR Y that reports the same exact head/base/S is accepted. state.mjs:352-359 validates the repair proof's S, N, H2 and effect result commit, but never validates proof.pr_number or binds it to the effect-bound repair merge attempt.input.prNumber. The parallel closure proof does enforce that relationship at state.mjs:313-323. Terminal validation at state.mjs:391-398 checks only the effect target and state, so the contradictory repair PR identity reaches remoteAdmissionStatus as a complete proof chain. This violates the required exact provider-effect reconciliation and P/E/H2/S proof binding despite passing gates.

The frozen real-temporary-Git/fake-provider suite exercises publish/readiness, merge/squash/rebase lineage including hidden earlier edges and legitimate multi-commit rebases, advanced M with fresh gates/review/verification, normal and raced P/E/H closure, mode conflicts, H2/S repair, all-stage interruption behavior, completion, fresh-process evidence continuation and next-story admission. The installed complete operation points to shipping.md, and pm.mjs exposes every documented low-level route. However, every repair reconciliation test passes the same PR number used by the retained repair merge attempt; no test supplies a distinct PR identity with the same reported exact Git effect. Consequently the suite does not detect the public AC2 defect and does not prove the full exact remote lifecycle. A bounded regression should retain repair merge effect PR X, reconcile PR Y through reconcileRemoteHandoffRepair with an otherwise identical exact S/base response, and require rejection with unchanged record bytes.

findings.message: current-pm.mjs validateAdmissionRecord/remoteAdmissionStatus accepts syntactically coherent completion without the required remote proof chain. It checks remote.version, optional slots only if present, completion target/branch/commit, then marks COMPLETE when commit is ancestor of HEAD. A record can omit source publication/merge proof, integration_evidence finalization, closure/handoff-repair proof and terminal artifact identities yet release admission. This directly violates initial-observations admission-proof ('syntactically valid completion.status alone cannot release hold').

closure/repair provider interruption is not implemented. reconcileExecutingAttempt is called only by source publish/merge. Closure executeProviderAttempt leaves thrown executing slots stuck; closure reconcile proves Git without settling the slot. Repair uses a bespoke runner that unconditionally allocates a new token whenever effect is null, overwriting an executing active token and permitting a second write; repair reconcile also never settles slots. This violates the all-stage prepared/executing/observed and read-only recovery contract. Fresh-process lost execution must remain UNKNOWN absent exact effect adoption; same-process ended+exact absence may replay the same token.

raced closure preimage checks compare only file text/hash, not Git mode. A concurrent 100644→100755 mode change on a P/E/H path has identical committedText, is allowed as an in-scope changed path, then wrapper restores H's mode; code accepts it, overwriting the advanced-base entry despite exact-preimage requirement.

H2 adoption compares only captureGitAnchor().protected_hash; unlike closure/completion it retains no protectedIgnoredEntries checkout proof, so worktree-local ignored protected metadata can drift between prepare/adopt without refusal.

maybeSupersedeSourceAttempt changes old.disposition/superseded_by then refreshAttempt(old), but deliberately leaves slot.effect unchanged. Its effect.attempt_identity therefore points to the pre-mutation identity that no retained attempt now has. The supersession proof omits required predecessor attempt/effect identities and validateProviderSlot never checks reciprocal links/effect-to-attempt binding. After successor success old effect pointer is replaced, so old identity is not durably recoverable.

rebase proof sets rebaseBase=parents[0] of final rebased commit and checks only rebaseBase..mergeCommit; for legitimate multi-commit source rebase, that parent is the preceding rebased source commit, so earlier rebased commits are outside bounded-path proof. Established premerge base is retained in merge attempt observation and should anchor the whole first-parent range. Current tests use one source commit.

claimCurrentPm checks remote admission before entering transact but does not repeat it inside the transaction, contrary to the approved T05B admission dispatch. A remote record can become applicable in another checkout after the precheck and before the story write, and the claim then commits without the required hold.

validateRemoteEnvelope validates only provider-slot shells and retry range, while prepareRemoteClosureCheckout trusts truthy integration_evidence.finalized/finalization. It does not validate the identified finalization or its binding to the current snapshot, gates, review and verification; a malformed/rebound record can therefore enter P/E/H closure with forged finalized evidence.

source merge interruption treats `MERGE_PENDING` as an absence state eligible for same-process replay (`mergeRemoteSource` passes `absenceStates: ['MERGE_PENDING']`). The frozen dispatch says replay requires exact provider absence and that open/queued remains pending; an open/queued PR may already retain a provider merge request, so it cannot prove no effect and must not authorize a second merge write. This needs to stay pending/read-only unless exact merge effect is adopted.

prepareRemoteHandoff does not require an adopted story-closure E. remotePrepareArtifact assigns `parent = closure.commit`, which can be null, persists the handoff pending record, then writes H bytes. Adoption can never accept a real commit whose parent equals null, and the dirty H write then prevents preparing E, leaving the workflow wedged. The public operation should refuse before record/file mutation until E is adopted.

For a normal closure, state.mjs:313-323 allows state `proven` while terminal_commit differs from the provider-bound merge_commit; rebinding that proof and completion together to a later commit that preserves the story/handoff entries can release admission even though the exact provider R was different. mergeRemoteSource does not implement the fix2 terminal fast path. After a source merge effect or source proof exists, it still calls remoteObservation/provider.inspect before executeProviderAttempt returns the retained effect. A same-input completed merge therefore depends on fresh provider and Git reads and can fail when the provider is unavailable, despite already having a durable result. T05B-fix2-design.json and T05B-supersession-dispatch.md require the successful merge to veto inspection, allocation and writes while preserving the same-input proven result.

Handoff-repair replacements generate a stale BASE_COMMIT. After HANDOFF_BASE_RACE, prepareHandoffRepair correctly selects latest.race_proof.terminal_commit as the new repairBase and pending parent, but remoteArtifactGeneration still receives closureCommit=closure.terminal_commit. The public retry therefore creates H2 as a direct child of the latest N while its handoff bytes name the original closure terminal. Resume and adoption repeat the same stale generation input, and completion later refuses the result. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:31 requires each replacement H2 to use BASE_COMMIT N for its actual latest proved parent.

Remote verification-report preparation can overwrite existing project reports. architecture-state.md:216 says P adds only docs/verification/<story-id>.md and docs/checklists/verification-<story-id>.md, and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:25 retains the existing P contract. prepareRemoteVerificationReport passes those paths to materializeRemoteWrites, which accepts non-null committed before-images. When a fetched advanced M already contains either path, the public P operation replaces it instead of refusing before durable preparation.

Remote artifact generation is not independently bound to its parent or retained after adoption. validateRemoteGeneration regenerates report/closure bytes from generation.inputs.story_before supplied by the descriptor itself but never requires that story to equal the committed parent story or pending write.before, nor does it require the retained source contract/execution identity. A coherently reidentified same-contract, different-Execution descriptor can therefore resume and adopt an E that is not the legal transition from its parent. remoteAdoptArtifact then discards the generation descriptor and records only field/commit/parent/tree/writes, so terminal P/E/H proof no longer names the source proof or remote finalization that generated it. This violates remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 and :25, which require receipts and closure preparation to remain bound to fetched M and its finalization.

Remote artifact publication does not preserve executable Git mode. materializeRemoteWrites retains expected_mode, but applyPending writes through atomic, whose replacement file is created mode 0600, and never restores the owner's executable bit. A valid 100755 story or handoff therefore becomes 100644 during E, H or H2 preparation and cannot pass adoption's exact expected-mode check. Pending recovery also compares only text, so same-text executable-mode drift on an owned path is accepted as resumable. The existing P/E/H entry contract and remote state schema explicitly support both 100644 and 100755.

Remote terminal evidence validation does not establish exact acceptance coverage or independent actors. validateRemotePublicationRecord accepts any nonempty all-PASS verification criteria without matching their IDs exactly to source.packet.acceptance, and it does not enforce that the remote reviewer and verifier differ from the builder and each other or that required panel coverage remains present. Reidentifying a same-snapshot verification with one invented PASS criterion and colliding actors still permits finalization, closure and terminal admission. T05B-AC2 and remote-lifecycle-interface.md:19 require fresh independent review and distinct complete verification bound to M.

A retained provider replay proof is not bound to the attempt target. validateRemoteProviderSlot checks that replay.absence_result is identified PR_ABSENT evidence and binds its invocation token, but does not require absence_result.expectedHead to equal attempt.input.target.expectedHead. A reidentified replay transition can therefore claim exact absence for a different head and later support a terminal provider chain. remote-lifecycle-interface.md:9 requires exact attempt inputs and result identity before same-token replay.

remoteAdmissionStatus reports the wrong terminal field before completion preparation. It selects value.remote.closure.proof.commit, but remote-closure-proof-v1 retains merge_commit and terminal_commit. A normal or stale REMOTE_CLOSURE_PROVEN record consequently returns remote_terminal_commit:null until a completion token exists, contrary to the exact remote-admission-status projection in T05B-operation-dispatch.md.

The declared npm test gate did not complete for the frozen fix2 candidate: it terminated with ETIMEDOUT at 600 seconds. Packaging validation passed, the candidate snapshot remained unchanged, and no orphan test processes remained, but a timed-out gate is not a PASS and cannot establish T05B acceptance.

criteria.evidence: At frozen snapshot 009feeee3ea2fee4433de2815ca869f6a54f74b186103a95ec0c902ca29a8c9f, I inspected the actual adapter and fake-runner tests. remote.mjs SHA-256 ba21914d8a131532ec38c66e40948621da9d81452449024d59ba5a837a10ea89 validates one fetch/push destination and auth, pushes only EXPECTED_HEAD:refs/heads/STORY_BRANCH at lines 599-617, binds the exact PR head/base, requires structured passing/skipping checks plus a fresh clean mergeable view, invokes gh pr merge with --match-head-commit at lines 672-704, and accepts a full merge OID only after exact remote-base inspection. remote.test.mjs SHA-256 8b3f797e85fdbaeadad3a457232050d156d0bbaadbd02cbba3173d394af40d82 uses an injected command runner and contains explicit missing-auth, pending/failed/unknown-check, head-race, rejected/queued/mismatched-merge, exact/advanced reconciliation and deleted-head recovery cases without real provider/model calls. The declared npm test gate itself did not pass: it timed out at 600 seconds before reaching these adapter tests, so this PASS rests on inspected criterion-specific source and test artifacts, not a claimed full-suite pass. Gate log SHA-256 d0a17b4e7b1e4c7b005f189e6bfa9db29d739d15a17153fb89b1c7bb5137d3c0.

The fix2 source resolves the five fix1 findings in their reported forms, including provider transition legality, supersession limits, terminal PR/commit cross-links and effect-bound N for merge/squash/rebase. The actual public lifecycle still violates the frozen contract in several reachable paths. Most directly, remote-lifecycle-interface.md:31 requires every replacement H2 to descend latest N and contain BASE_COMMIT N. reconcileRemoteHandoffRepair persists a raced terminal and increments retry at integration.mjs:2964-2977; the next prepare uses it as repairBase and pending.parent at :2806 and :2828-2831, but generates H2 with the original closure.terminal_commit at :2820-2822. handoffContent writes that stale value at :3500-3509. Resume/adopt validate the same stale basis at :2800-2802 and :2860-2862, while adoptRemoteCompletion later requires the latest repair proof.parent at :3027, so authorized retries 1 and 2 cannot complete. Remote artifact materialization also records expected_mode but atomic write replaces files as mode 0600 without restoring it (:2486-2501, :590-596, :3473-3485), making a valid 100755 story/handoff unadoptable and allowing same-text mode drift through pending recovery. prepareRemoteVerificationReport at :2594-2598 can overwrite existing report/checklist paths although architecture-state.md:216-221 requires P to add them and local P rejects existing paths at :3718-3732. remoteAdmissionStatus projects closure.proof.commit at current-pm.mjs:415 even though closure proof stores merge_commit/terminal_commit, so a proved normal closure reports a null remote terminal. The formal npm test gate is also FAIL due to ETIMEDOUT at 600 seconds; npm run validate passed.

The frozen fake-provider/temporary-Git suite connects public API/CLI operations and covers normal and raced closure, initial H2/S repair, interruption, completion and retry counting, but it does not prove the full implemented user lifecycle. In tests/remote-lifecycle.test.mjs:2685-2737 the replacement-retry loop asserts retry number, parent and exhaustion only; it never asserts replacement H2 BASE_COMMIT or completes adoption after a replacement race. The initial attempt alone asserts BASE_COMMIT at :2407. Tests also lack the executable-mode pending/recovery boundary and remote-P existing-path refusal described in AC2. The only formal current-snapshot test run timed out after 600 seconds before the remote lifecycle and adapter files completed, with status FAIL and log SHA-256 d0a17b4e7b1e4c7b005f189e6bfa9db29d739d15a17153fb89b1c7bb5137d3c0; validation passed with log SHA-256 8b146bfab36098ddfe081ce34555566bdef41fef310ead7321bad3fa329549f0. Snapshot/run state remained unchanged at run revision 14.
